newsitem.title: USA: Pennzoil Q2 net drops under $11.7mln charge.
newsitem.headline: Pennzoil Q2 net drops under $11.7mln charge.

text.p: Pennzoil Co said Monday its second-quarter recurring income increased 44 percent to $35.6 million, or $0.76 a share, with all its business segments improving their operating income.

But, including after-tax charges totaling $11.7 million, the company's net dropped to $23.9 million, or $0.51 a share, in the quarter, compared with a $24.5 million net, or $0.53 a share, the year before.
A First Call consensus estimate of 11 brokers had expected the company to earn $0.69 a share in the quarter.

Pennzoil said the $11.7 million charge related to selling its PennUnion natural gas marketing unit, paying down debt, and "costs incurred in connection with Union Pacific Resources unsolicited tender offer."

Chief executive James Pate said in a statement Pennzoil's seven consecutive quarters of year-over-year increases in recurring earnings "reflected the company's transformation to an operationally focused company."
The company' cash flow from operations increased 12 percent to $132.4 million, or $2.82 per share, compared to $118.3 million, or $2.55 per share, the year before.

Pennzoil's oil and gas division operating income rose five percent to $69.1 million in the quarter, from $65.5 million. The company attributed the rise to higher natural gas prices and lower general and administrative expenses and taxes, which were partially offset by lower production and higher depreciation rates and operating expenses.

Oil production decreased to 62,781 barrels a day (bpd), from 65,009 bpd. Production rose about five percent, excluding the 11,200 bpd output net to the Canadian properties which Pennzoil sold in July 1996.

The company's motor oil and refined products division's operating income jumped 63 percent to $25.8 million, from $15.8 million last year. Pennzoil ascribed the rise to higher margins resulting from upgrading its Shreveport refinery and higher income from its Excel Paralubes lube base oil plant joint venture.
Pennzoil said its Jiffy Lube International Inc franchises' operating income increased 19 percent to $6.3 million in the quarter because of lower expenses at company-operated stores.
The company's stock traded at 77-15/16 Monday morning, down 1/16.
